name: narrative-lens
description: narrative-lens reads a passage or a whole manuscript and returns structured, explainable judgments about the writing: readability grades, pacing and syntax tension, dialogue extraction, voice drift between a character's earlier and later lines, whether a setup planted early pays off later, and whether a chapter contradicts an established timeline or world state. Every result carries a confidence score and, where the analysis supports it, the evidence that produced it. It is deterministic, runs entirely on the user's machine with no language model and no network call, and ships as a Rust crate and a Node.js package with generated TypeScript types. It was extracted from the meaning engine of Emathy, a macOS authoring app, so that any manuscript tool can reuse the same analyzers.
description_good_justification: README.md opens with a one-sentence description of what the software does and who it is for: "Local, deterministic prose and narrative-craft analysis: readability, pacing, voice, foreshadowing, continuity, with no LLM and no network call.". The same description is in Cargo.toml and package.json.
interact_justification: README.md has Install (crates.io and npm), API, and Contributing sections; CONTRIBUTING.md explains how to set up a development environment and open a pull request; feedback goes through GitHub Issues at https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-lens/issues.
contribution_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md describes the process: clone, build, run the Rust and Node test suites, then open a pull request against main; pull requests are reviewed through GitHub.
contribution_requirements_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md states the acceptance requirements: `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` must pass; new analyzers include a test against a realistic passage with an independently authored expected result; public API changes regenerate bindings/ via `cargo test --features bindings` and update docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
floss_license_justification: Apache License 2.0, declared as license = "Apache-2.0" in Cargo.toml and package.json, with the full text in LICENSE.
license_location_justification: The complete Apache-2.0 text is in LICENSE at the repository root, and GitHub's license detection identifies it as Apache-2.0.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md covers installation, what the software analyzes, the API, requirements, and development; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md explains the design and docs/INTEGRATION.md shows how to use the library from other tools.
documentation_interface_justification: The Node interface is fully typed in index.d.ts, generated from the Rust types with ts-rs; every public Rust item carries a doc comment and the crate builds with rustdoc (documentation = https://docs.rs/narrative-lens).
sites_https_justification: The project site and repository are https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-lens (HTTPS). The package pages https://www.npmjs.com/package/narrative-lens and https://crates.io/crates/narrative-lens are HTTPS.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues at https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-lens/issues is the discussion mechanism: searchable, URL-addressable, usable from any browser with a free GitHub account, no proprietary client required.
english_justification: README.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, SECURITY.md, docs/*.md, code comments, and commit messages are written in English.
maintained_justification: The repository has had commits within the last month (October 2026), Dependabot pull requests are reviewed and merged as they arrive, and bug reports are answered by the maintainer.
repo_track_justification: Git records author, date, and diff for every change; git log shows named authors for every commit.
repo_interim_justification: Interim commits are pushed to main continuously between releases.
repo_distributed_justification: Git is a distributed version control system.
version_unique_justification: Cargo.toml and package.json both declare version 0.1.0; each release is a unique semantic version.
version_semver_justification: Versions follow Semantic Versioning (0.1.0 today) as recorded in Cargo.toml, package.json, and CHANGELOG.md, which states adherence to SemVer.
version_tags_justification: The npm release 0.1.0 is tagged in git as v0.1.0 at the commit it was published from; future releases are tagged the same way.
release_notes_justification: CHANGELOG.md exists in Keep a Changelog format but only has an Unreleased section so far; the first GitHub Release with release notes has not been cut yet. The crate workflow (publish-crate.yml) runs from a GitHub Release, so notes will accompany each release going forward.
release_notes_vulns_justification: No publicly known vulnerability has been fixed in any release, so there are none to list.
report_process_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md and the README Contributing section direct bug reports to the GitHub issue tracker at https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-lens/issues, and SECURITY.md covers security reports separately.
report_tracker_justification: GitHub Issues at https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-lens/issues tracks each report individually with number, state, and labels.
report_responses_justification: No external bug report has been filed yet, so there is none left unanswered; the maintainer answers Dependabot pull requests as they arrive and will respond to reports through the issue tracker.
enhancement_responses_justification: No external enhancement request has been filed yet, so there is none left unanswered; the README lists the areas where contributions are wanted and the maintainer responds to issues as they arrive.
report_archive_justification: All issues and pull requests, with their responses, are publicly archived and searchable at https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-lens/issues?q=is%3Aissue.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: SECURITY.md (repository root) tells reporters to use GitHub private vulnerability reporting at https://github.com/writerslogic/narrative-lens/security/advisories/new or email security@writerslogic.com, and asks for reproduction steps and impact.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: SECURITY.md gives two private channels: GitHub private security advisories and security@writerslogic.com.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability report has been received yet, so there is nothing to measure against the 14-day target; SECURITY.md commits to acknowledging reports within 5 business days.
build_justification: The Rust library builds with `cargo build`; the Node addon builds with `npm run build` (napi-rs); both are documented in README.md and CONTRIBUTING.md and run in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml).
build_common_tools_justification: Cargo and npm, the standard tools for Rust and Node, are the only build tools.
build_floss_tools_justification: Cargo, rustc, Node, npm, and @napi-rs/cli are all FLOSS.
test_justification: Automated test suite: 596 Rust unit and integration tests (src/ and tests/craft.rs, structure.rs, continuity.rs with fixtures) run with `cargo test`; Node binding tests in tests/node run with `npm test` (node --test) plus a strict TypeScript check of the generated bindings (`npm run test:types`).
test_invocation_justification: `cargo test` and `npm test` run the whole suite with no manual steps; CONTRIBUTING.md and README.md document both.
test_most_justification: 596 Rust tests cover every analyzer in the craft, structure, and continuity categories against fixture passages; 5 Node tests exercise the binding surface end to end, and a strict TypeScript check validates the generated bindings.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs fmt, clippy, the Rust tests, the Node build and tests, and the TypeScript check on every push to main and every pull request.
test_policy_justification: CONTRIBUTING.md requires that new functionality comes with tests: new analyzers must include a test against a realistic passage whose expected result was authored independently of the implementation.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent feature commits add tests alongside the code (the initial extraction landed each analyzer with its own tests, and CONTRIBUTING.md makes a fixture test a condition for adding an analyzer).
tests_documented_added_justification: The test requirement is stated in CONTRIBUTING.md under "Before opening a PR".
warnings_justification: CI runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check`; rustc warnings are denied through the same clippy invocation.
warnings_fixed_justification: CI fails on any warning, so main carries zero rustc or clippy warnings.
warnings_strict_justification: `-D warnings` turns every rustc and clippy warning into an error in CI, and clippy runs with --all-targets.
know_secure_design_justification: The maintainer applies secure design principles: the library is a pure function from text to a result, with no network, no filesystem access beyond an explicitly supplied model path, no shared mutable state, and input bounds enforced on sizes (see SECURITY.md and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).
know_common_errors_justification: The maintainer is familiar with common error classes (injection, memory safety, integer overflow, denial of service through unbounded input). Rust's type system and the absence of unsafe code address memory safety; inputs are bounded.
crypto_published_justification: The project implements no cryptographic functionality.
crypto_call_justification: The project implements no cryptographic functionality.
crypto_floss_justification: The project implements no cryptographic functionality.
crypto_keylength_justification: The project implements no cryptographic functionality.
crypto_working_justification: The project implements no cryptographic functionality.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The project implements no cryptographic functionality.
crypto_pfs_justification: The project implements no network protocols.
crypto_password_storage_justification: The project stores no passwords or credentials.
crypto_random_justification: The project generates no security-relevant random values.
delivery_mitm_justification: Releases are delivered through the npm registry and crates.io over HTTPS with registry-side integrity hashes; source is delivered from GitHub over HTTPS.
delivery_unsigned_justification: npm packages are published with npm provenance (Sigstore attestations linking the package to the GitHub Actions run), which npm verifies on install, so a man-in-the-middle cannot substitute an unsigned package.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No open medium-or-higher vulnerability is known. Dependabot alerts, Dependabot updates, and cargo-deny advisory checks (deny.toml) are enabled so any new one is surfaced promptly.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No unpatched critical vulnerability has been reported.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: The repository contains no credentials; publishing tokens live in GitHub Actions secrets and CI uses OIDC provenance.
static_analysis_justification: Two static analysers run in CI on every pull request: clippy with -D warnings (.github/workflows/ci.yml) and CodeQL for Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, and GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/codeql.yml). OpenSSF Scorecard runs weekly (.github/workflows/scorecard.yml).
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: CodeQL's security query suite looks for common vulnerabilities in the Rust and JavaScript code on every pull request and on a weekly schedule.
static_analysis_fixed_justification: There are no open CodeQL or clippy findings; CI fails on any clippy finding, and CodeQL results are reviewed in the repository's code scanning tab.
static_analysis_often_justification: clippy and CodeQL run on every pull request and every push to main.
dynamic_analysis_justification: No fuzzer or other dynamic analysis is wired up yet. The analyzers are pure functions over text, so a cargo-fuzz target is the planned next step; this criterion is suggested rather than required.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic analysis runs yet, so there is nothing to enable assertions in. This criterion is suggested rather than required.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The project is written in Rust with zero `unsafe` blocks (grep -rn unsafe src returns nothing), so it is not written in a memory-unsafe language.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic analysis has reported a vulnerability.
